title: Market Research
description: Research a product, analyze customer material you supply, or see how competing offers and ads are positioned.

modes.title: Research a product
modes.description: Start with a product, target market, and decision. Get source-linked findings and a handoff for creative and the store.

steps.title: Set the product and decision
steps.instruction: Set up the Evolve product overview for the selected product, market, and decision. Reuse the supplied saved research and brief, retaining its evidence IDs and dates. Separate current verified product facts and offer terms, seller assertions, assumptions, and gaps. Specify which gaps could change the decision and which sources can fill them.
checks: The product, market, decision and relevant offer are explicit or identified as missing.
Reused facts preserve source IDs, and assumptions and seller claims are distinguished from verified facts.

steps.title: Collect customer and competitor evidence
steps.instruction: Do the evidence collection section of the Evolve full-product route only. Inspect accessible first-party facts, independent buyer language, competing offers, ad examples, and failed alternatives. Give each item a stable evidence ID, source URL or filename, date or observation date, relevant excerpt and limitation. Deduplicate repeated reviews, retain contradictions, classify swipe sources by use, and record gaps where public or account material is unavailable. Use only the approved sources available to this run. Diagnose awareness and sophistication with supporting evidence before the mechanism and information passes.
checks: Findings are traceable to inspected evidence or explicitly marked as inference or a gap.
Contradictions, duplicates, sample limits and the difference between observed competitor activity and measured performance are accounted for.

steps.title: Find and rank buying desires
steps.instruction: Run only the first original Evolve pass, Desire Hunt, from the full product research route. Verify and use the exact original when available, with product context and known angles supplied separately. Capture distinct ranked desires, exact customer language and stable evidence IDs. Report the prompt source and any unavailable inputs. Where the portable pack lacks the original, label the sourced findings as a focused fallback and keep the exact pass marked incomplete.
checks: Separate desires from product features and angles, retaining evidence IDs and counterexamples.
Record actual prompt provenance and scope; an unavailable original is never counted as completed.

steps.title: Check new mechanisms
steps.instruction: Run only the second original Evolve pass, New Mechanisms, using the source map and Market Sophistication document, verified product facts and earlier evidence. Evaluate the problem mechanism and product mechanism separately at the observed sophistication level. Explain which links are established and which need proof. If the original is missing, mark the exact pass incomplete and label any focused mechanism analysis separately.
checks: Mechanisms have a traceable factual basis or a specific proof gap, regardless of market sophistication.
Mechanism recommendations explain how the solution would answer the identified problem, with uncertainty preserved.

steps.title: Find and verify new information
steps.instruction: Run only the third original Evolve pass, New Information, with the unmodified original when available. Use dated firsthand or primary sources where accessible. For each result, state what is new to this market, where it comes from, and which creative decision it changes. If nothing qualifies, name the gap. If the original is missing, mark the exact pass incomplete and label any focused findings separately.
checks: Every new fact has a source, date, scope and implication, or an explicit reason the cell remains empty.
The result does not confuse recency, novelty, interpretation or an example in the course with verified product evidence.

steps.title: Turn evidence into buyer insights
steps.instruction: Use the earlier evidence and desire, mechanism and information reports to fill the relevant Research to Ad fields before drafting angles. Define the core buyer, meaningful sub-avatars, their shared desire and the different situation, objection, or proof requirement that warrants a distinct ad. If manual VOC is supplied, reconcile its independently coded evidence and contradictions before finalizing profiles. Record awareness, sophistication, belief shift, failed alternatives, proof needs and remaining unknowns.
checks: Each retained profile or belief links to specific evidence IDs and the practical messaging consequence.
Each distinct sub-avatar warrants a distinct ad, and unresolved claims never move into the approved proof list.

steps.title: Develop and rank ad angles
steps.instruction: Run only the fourth original Evolve research pass, Ad Angles, using the retained sub-avatars and prior evidence. When the original is available, preserve the full prompt and examples and supply working inputs separately. Rank three angles per retained profile and three hooks or headlines per angle when evidence permits. Name the first test, the reason for its priority, the pattern used, and the source IDs and claim boundaries. If the original is missing, label the exact pass incomplete and identify any focused fallback.
checks: Angle and hook choices derive from established profiles and source IDs and include an explicit test priority.
Unknown material is indicated instead of filling the requested count with weak or unsupported variants.

steps.title: Deliver the reusable research record
steps.instruction: Assemble the passed research reports without repeating the collection or the four prompt passes. Include the evidence register and coverage limits, a receipt for the actual course prompts consulted, and the strongest and conflicting buyer, competitor and account evidence. End with a clearly labeled Creative Grounding Pack covering the product, market and offer, target buyer, locked or ranked desire, awareness, sophistication, the market gap, mechanism pair, One Belief, proof, permitted and unsupported claims, selected angle or options, VOC IDs, destination continuity and first test. Give the research record a date and product scope. Identify any formal Evolve course report or worksheets still outstanding if this local report run cannot produce them.
checks: The assembled report retains the evidence record and the order and actual completion status of the four original passes.
A creator can reuse the handoff with its exact facts, proof gaps, buyer and test objective without redoing the research.

modes.title: Analyze customer material I provide
modes.description: Use your pasted reviews, interviews or comments. Get an evidence register and a short list of testable findings.

steps.title: Index the source language
steps.instruction: Process the supplied customer material independently before reading or reconciling any summaries. Preserve exact brief excerpts, surrounding context, stable source IDs, dates and source types when present. Deduplicate repeated copies while retaining counterexamples. Code observed triggers, frustrations, workarounds, objections, desire, and awareness. Mark secondhand material and opt to report the actual sample rather than making population claims. If there are zero customer records to index, identify that missing input and request a review, customer message or attributed interview note before synthesis.
checks: At least one inspectable customer record with identifiable provenance is present. A writer's example, seller claim, staff hypothesis or zero-record summary cannot satisfy this criterion. Rate it missing when no customer material was supplied.
Every shared customer excerpt is faithful to supplied wording and linked to its source.
Deduplication, contradictory evidence and sample limits are explicit.

steps.title: Update the product findings
steps.instruction: Synthesize the indexed voice of customer into distinct themes and opportunity territories. Compare with any saved research and identify what the new evidence confirms, challenges or leaves unresolved. Keep original wording and source IDs in the update. Return a dated handoff containing the most plausible buyer, desire and next research or test decision. Keep unsourced interpretations separate from directly observed material.
checks: Major themes can be traced back to the indexed corpus, including relevant counterexamples.
The handoff says what changed, why it matters for the product decision, and what still requires proof.

modes.title: Research competitors
modes.description: Start with competitor names or links. Get a comparable offer map and a separate teardown of ads you can inspect.

steps.title: Compare offers and alternatives
steps.instruction: Build dated profiles grouped by direct competitors and substitutes. Record market, currency, observed or supplied price, pack size, terms, promise, apparent mechanism, proof, landing destination and source for material facts. Make like-for-like comparisons and mark inaccessible details. Reuse existing dated profiles only where still relevant to the decision.
checks: Comparisons account for market, date, currency and effective unit or bundle size when relevant.
Visible assertions and terms are attributed accurately without treating them as verified efficacy.

steps.title: Find transferable creative patterns
steps.instruction: Use the offer profiles and ads that can actually be inspected. Capture dated ad references, hook and beat structure, visual device, proof and destination. Classify separate swipes as cross-niche structure, direct-competitor message territory, or organic format. Identify the saturated message and one buyer-relevant gap with evidence or mark the gap provisional. Suggest an original hypothesis grounded in the user's research. Treat longevity, reach and observed activity as leads.
checks: Each recommendation distinguishes observed creative, performance evidence or its absence, and proposed execution.
A pattern has a stated use, supporting sources and a proof requirement before transfer to another product.

modes.title: Review my ad account evidence
modes.description: Use an authorized first-party export and sample creatives. Get a comparable baseline for future tests.

steps.title: Establish the creative baseline
steps.instruction: Match supplied creatives and ad IDs to the export and attribution window. Compare spend, reach, conversions and performance over compatible periods. Flag thin samples, mixed attribution and absent metrics. Name controls by the available evidence and identify a realistic one-variable test. Return source IDs and gaps for the creative brief.
checks: The baseline uses actual compatible first-party inputs and clearly marks missing or inconclusive metrics.
Each proposed control and test can be traced to a creative ID and an observable metric or caveat.

title: Copywriting & Briefs
description: Turn product research into an angle, an Evolve creative brief, placement-ready copy or a spoken video script.

modes.title: Find an angle to test
modes.description: Use your product research and get a ranked shortlist of distinct reasons to buy.

steps.title: Rank evidence-backed angles
steps.instruction: Start with the existing buyer and desire findings. Use the original Evolve Ad Angles method when available and disclose the actual source. Rank angles that express distinct reasons to buy or distinct ways to activate a locked desire. For each, include buyer, triggering situation, angle, evidence IDs, claim boundaries, hook direction and predicted response. Propose the first test and its independent variable.
checks: Angles are strategically distinct within the requested scope, and relevant claims and test variables are grounded in the research.
Recommendations preserve any existing desire or audience lock.

modes.title: Write a creative brief
modes.description: Use an angle or an existing reference. Get the matching Evolve brief for an original ad, adaptation or variation.

steps.title: Complete the Evolve brief
steps.instruction: Pick the matching original Evolve brief: Ideation for a new concept, Imitation for a swipe, or Iteration for a measured parent ad. Preserve the template fields and identify the original consulted. Reuse the dated product research and any user-locked angle. Record buyer, desire, awareness, idea, format, hook direction, promise, source IDs, supported proof, claim limits, offer, destination, CTA and test objective. For adaptation, note what the reference contributes. For iteration, include the retained controls and the one proposed change. Mark proposed decisions as such and never assume approval.
checks: The route and the brief fields match the evidence, objective and intended format.
Downstream creative can reuse the approved product facts, buyer, desire, proof and test objective without guessing.

modes.title: Write and review ad copy
modes.description: Bring a product brief and placement. Get reviewed copy you can use in the ad.

steps.title: Draft for the selected placement
steps.instruction: Use the supplied Evolve brief or clearly label a provisional brief when critical inputs are missing. Route to the original Evolve writing method for this placement when available. Keep the buyer, desire, angle, claim limits and offer fixed. Make each hook or format change deliberate. Return a complete draft and a separate source map for substantive claims, proof, testimonials and offer terms.
checks: Draft follows the requested placement and conveys the same promise and test hypothesis as the brief.
No factual claim, statistic, testimonial, scarcity or offer term exceeds the provided evidence.

steps.title: Check claims, clarity and voice
steps.instruction: Read the entire draft in order using the original Evolve line-review criteria where available. Check specificity, buyer relevance, mechanism, proof, offer, reason to buy, mobile readability and continuity into the destination. Keep a short change log linking exact lines to the reason and evidence. Apply a voice polish only when useful and preserve verbatim sourced customer language and locked decisions. Return a clean placement-ready copy block separate from review notes and remaining gaps.
checks: The review identifies concrete issues or confirms why the relevant lines work.
The revised copy preserves the offer, claim limits and designated test variables and is usable for the selected placement.

modes.title: Fix specific lines in my draft
modes.description: Bring copy, its audience and the desired action. Get a diagnosis and targeted revisions.

steps.title: Diagnose and rewrite the weak lines
steps.instruction: Use the Evolve copy review method for the supplied draft, check against the brief and available sources, and return exact original lines, the issue, the smallest effective revision and the rationale. Supply a consolidated clean version where requested. Preserve substantiated facts, offer, voice and control placements, and call out unsupported claims with a needed proof or a grounded replacement.
checks: The review stays within the requested edit scope and cites the original lines it diagnoses.
Suggested revisions improve specificity, momentum or proof without adding unsupported assertions.

modes.title: Write a one-take voice-over script
modes.description: Use an angle, desire, concrete subject and exact hook. Get a camera-ready script with the three-act structure from the supplied example.

steps.title: Lock the angle, desire, facts and hook
steps.instruction: Set up the relevant Evolve brief and the one-take format separately. Record the exact supplied opening hook, one angle, one desire, and the concrete subject to teach. Mark a suggested hook or other assumption explicitly if it was not supplied. Build a line-level ledger of usable facts, mechanism, proof, and genuine firsthand experience if supplied. Identify the one functional need that bridges from the problem to the product. Flag example claims or requested visuals that lack evidence.
checks: The exact supplied hook is present and the other three inputs are explicit, or the missing input is clearly identified.
The plan uses one camera-facing speaker and distinguishes product truth, example material and missing substantiation.

steps.title: Write the three-act spoken draft
steps.instruction: Use the verified brief and the one-take format to write the script as numbered spoken sentences with one sentence per line. Aim for 12 to 16 sentences, using the evidence to determine act lengths without filler or compression. Act 1 opens with the exact supplied hook, then teaches the issue through specific, sourced facts and a plain analogy if it clarifies the evidence. Keep brand and product out of Acts 1 and 2. Act 2 is exactly one sentence and states the specific functional need. The first line of Act 3 names the actual product and explains how its supported mechanism meets that need. Close by returning to the original emotion with a simple link CTA. Use grounded speech. Separate optional visuals and production notes from the spoken lines, and keep them compatible with one continuous performance.
checks: The spoken hook is exact, Acts 1 and 2 are product-free, the bridge is one sentence, and the first line of Act 3 introduces the product.
The technical explanation uses only grounded facts and any personal experience is supplied or phrased without invented testimony.

steps.title: Review the mechanism and evidence
steps.instruction: Audit each factual spoken line and any optional shot against the locked evidence. Assess whether the education actually establishes the need, the single bridge is specific, and the mechanism answers it. Identify implied claims and unsupported first-person results. Compare the performance features against the available step-by-step reference, including early concreteness, length, mechanism clarity and emotional payoff, treating the example as a format and voice reference. Return the revised script and a concise record of fixes. Preserve the supplied hook while flagging any evidence issue it contains for the user to resolve.
checks: Material facts and visuals trace to the evidence, and any unresolved claim is visible for approval.
The corrected bridge and mechanism answer the same need, and the comparison covers structure without inheriting example facts.

steps.title: Check the read aloud and deliver
steps.instruction: Read the corrected script as one speaker talking to a phone. Open with the supplied hook and a concrete thing the viewer can picture early. Show separate headings for Act 1, Act 2 and Act 3, with one spoken sentence on each numbered line and exactly one functional bridge sentence in Act 2. Introduce the product only in Act 3. Remove redundant lines. Express the audience's frustration and payoff through an observable action, prop or moment when the brief supports one, and bring it back just before the link. Do not invent a testimonial or a result. Keep only facts needed for the demo or requested by the user; combine required offer facts into natural speech. Replace awkward spoken caveats with an observable detail when it does the same teaching job. Keep evidence limits and visual notes outside the spoken copy. Preserve the hook, grounded mechanism, required approved wording and CTA intent. Return the clean script and a brief comparison of structure, spoken rhythm and payoff, citing actual lines if a step-by-step reference was supplied.
checks: Act 1, Act 2 and Act 3 are explicitly labeled. The exact hook opens Act 1; Act 2 is one functional bridge sentence; the product enters in Act 3. Numbered speech has one sentence per line and sounds natural without filler, catalog-style lists or repeated mechanism statements.
The closing earns the CTA through a concrete callback to the opening problem where the brief supports it. The product explanation remains accurate, and any comparison uses an available reference.
